memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelek, and the two men made a treaty. Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs from the flock, and Abimelek asked him, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs you have set apart by themselves?" He replied, "Accept these seven lambs from my hand as a witness that I dug this well." - Gen 21:27-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham and Abimelech make a treaty - a covenant of peace between them. Abraham gives gifts, sets apart seven lambs as a witness, and establishes his rightful claim to the well he had dug. What began as a dispute (v.25) ends in a formal agreement of peace and mutual respect. Two men who could have become enemies choose instead to become covenant partners.

There is real wisdom in this. Abraham took deliberate, concrete steps to secure peace. He didn't leave the relationship in a state of unresolved tension; he acted to establish clarity, fairness, and goodwill. Peacemaking is not passive - it takes effort, generosity, and intentional action.

Notice Abraham's generosity in the process. He gives sheep and cattle, freely offering gifts to seal the peace. Peace is often costly; it requires us to give, to yield, to invest in the relationship rather than merely defending our own interests. Abraham was willing to pay the price of peace.

This reflects the heart of God, who is "the God of peace" (Rom 15:33) and who went to the greatest cost of all to make peace with us. Through the cross, God made a covenant of peace with sinners, giving His own Son to reconcile us to Himself (Col 1:20). As people who have received such peace, we are called to be peacemakers, taking concrete, sometimes costly steps to live at peace with others. "If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone" (Rom 12:18).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you taking concrete steps toward peace in your relationships?
- Where might God be calling you to pay the cost of peacemaking?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
God of peace, thank You for the costly peace You made with me through the cross. Make me a peacemaker who takes concrete, sometimes costly steps toward reconciliation. Help me live at peace with everyone, as far as I can.
Amen.
